lessons.title: Why we coach
lessons.summary: Start with the individual child and the environment they experience.

lessons.title: Enter their world
lessons.summary: Notice, listen and respond to the child in front of you.

lessons.title: Adapt the challenge
lessons.summary: Choose one change for one child, then see what happens.

lessons.title: Build a session around the child
lessons.summary: Connect a simple opening game, a purposeful progression and a whole game.

lessons.title: Reflect and develop
lessons.summary: Use a specific moment, the child’s voice and mentor feedback to shape your next session.

lessons.title: Support the lead coach
lessons.summary: Be a calm, clear extra adult with an agreed role and a route for help.

lessons.title: What the research tells us
lessons.summary: Explain why we observe, reflect, try and check again.

lessons.title: Choosing a mentoring method
lessons.summary: Choose support that fits the coach and return ownership.

lessons.title: Before the visit
lessons.summary: Confirm the arrangement, one focus and supervision.

lessons.title: During practice
lessons.summary: Observe facts, support briefly and hand back.

lessons.title: Supporting coaches during games
lessons.summary: Use the matchday card while the coach leads.

lessons.title: After the visit and into the next session
lessons.summary: Agree one next action and check what happened.

lessons.title: Recording support and following through
lessons.summary: Keep useful adult records and respect their limits.

resources.title: Soccer tag
resources.equipment: Proposed: balls for non-taggers, cones, goals or gates, pinnies.
resources.setup: Mark an area and scoring targets. Dimensions not specified.

resources.title: Sharks & Surfers
resources.players: 1–2 sharks; surfers each with a ball (source)
resources.equipment: Proposed: balls, cones, goals or gates, pinnies.
resources.setup: Beaches at the ends and ocean in the middle, as shown in the original diagram. Dimensions unspecified.

resources.title: Home & Away
resources.equipment: Proposed: several balls, cones, two colours of pinnies.
resources.setup: Divide area into two team halves. Balls start on halfway.

resources.title: Cops & Robbers
resources.players: 4 teams: 3 robber teams and 1 cop team (source)
resources.equipment: Proposed: balls, cones, four colours of pinnies.
resources.setup: Mark a central bank and team hideouts. Agree safe tagging.

resources.title: Hide & Seek
resources.equipment: Proposed: several balls, cones, goals, pinnies.
resources.setup: Give hiders balls in an area; identify seekers’ scoring targets. Dimensions unspecified.

resources.title: Piggy in the Middle / Hot Potato
resources.equipment: Cones with balls on top; proposed spare balls and boundary cones.
resources.setup: Split field into halves with target cones, following source diagram. Dimensions unspecified.

resources.title: Goalie Wars
resources.players: 2 teams; one active goalkeeper at each end (source)
resources.equipment: Goals and balls; proposed halfway cones and safe waiting areas.
resources.setup: Two halves, one goal each. Adjust distance and shot type with lead coach; dimensions unspecified.

resources.title: Risky Business
resources.equipment: 6 balls; proposed goals, cones and pinnies.
resources.setup: Attackers start at side; defenders split behind goals.

resources.title: Decisions, Decisions
resources.equipment: 5 balls per team; proposed goals, cones, pinnies.
resources.setup: Two fields back-to-back: midfield section 10–15 yards long, final section 5–8 yards, width 15–20 yards (source). Adjust to site and children.

resources.title: Build Up
resources.setup: Start players at goallines; dimensions unspecified.

resources.title: Waves
resources.players: 3 teams; 2–3 attackers versus 1 defender at a time (source)
resources.equipment: Proposed: balls, goals, cones, three colours of pinnies.
resources.setup: Two fields back-to-back: source suggests 10–15 yard midfield sections, 5–8 yard final sections, 15–20 yard width.

resources.title: 4v2 Rondo
resources.minutes: Not specified; proposed short rounds agreed with coach
resources.equipment: Proposed: ball, cones, pinnies, counterattack targets.
resources.setup: Mark area and counterattack targets with lead coach; size unspecified.

resources.title: 4v2 Keep & Switch
resources.minutes: Not specified; proposed short rounds agreed with coach
resources.equipment: Proposed: ball, cones, pinnies, counterattack targets.
resources.setup: Use original 4v2 arrangement. Agree what counts as a switch; dimensions unspecified.

resources.title: Three-team Rondo
resources.minutes: Not specified; proposed short rounds agreed with coach
resources.equipment: Proposed: ball, boundary cones, three colours of pinnies.
resources.setup: Attacking teams in separate halves; defenders start centrally.

resources.title: 1v1 Nanosoccer
resources.equipment: 2 goals per duel; proposed balls, cones, pinnies.
resources.setup: Separate parallel spaces and mark retreat line. Dimensions unspecified.

resources.title: Score & Move
resources.minutes: Not specified; proposed short rounds agreed with coach
resources.players: 2 teams over 2 fields; e.g. 2v2 or 3v3 per field (source)
resources.equipment: Proposed: two balls, goals, cones, pinnies.
resources.setup: Two adjacent fields, clear safe transfer route. Dimensions unspecified.

pathways.title: Me, my ball, my game
pathways.summary: Offer a simple start, room to explore and reassuring adult support. Age is a navigation aid; respond to the individual.

stages.title: Feel welcome and begin
stages.description: Notice confidence and offer a clear starting point.

stages.title: Try a decision against an opponent
stages.description: Observe time to look, turn and try again.

stages.title: Listen and adapt
stages.description: Ask what helped; repeat a useful game before adding complexity.

pathways.title: Explore, keep and share
pathways.summary: Retain individual involvement while introducing choices with a teammate.

stages.title: Find another player
stages.description: Offer reasons to connect while watching who remains involved.

pathways.title: My ball, our ball, our game
pathways.summary: Offer age-appropriate problems with flexible support and challenge.

stages.title: See the individual
stages.description: Begin with an accessible game and watch each child.

stages.title: Respond to change
stages.description: Notice possession, numbers and safe transitions.

pathways.title: Us and our game
pathways.summary: Connect individual choices to teammates without losing sight of each child.

stages.title: Read a situation
stages.description: Consider pressure, space and scoring choices.

stages.title: Support and transition
stages.description: Explore responses when the game changes.

stages.title: Keep and switch
stages.description: Offer an accessible passing problem; adjust for experience.

pathways.title: Build a team game
pathways.summary: Explore shared problems with individual roles, observation and feedback.

stages.title: Make a choice together
stages.description: Discuss options and hear quieter voices.

stages.title: Connect across space
stages.description: Watch support and switching, rather than counting passes alone.

stages.title: Transfer and reflect
stages.description: Use changing numbers and transition, then review one moment.

pathways.title: Observe → assist → lead with support
pathways.summary: A proposed phased pathway. Agree responsibilities and readiness with the lead coach and mentor.

stages.title: Observe and understand
stages.description: Read Why we coach and Enter their world. Shadow a lead coach and notice one child.

stages.title: Assist an agreed activity
stages.description: Complete Support the lead coach. Take one defined job, then discuss what helped children join.

stages.title: Lead a short part with supervision
stages.description: Agree an activity and briefing. Mentor observes, gives feedback and agrees the next responsibility.

tasks.title: Understand one child
tasks.prompt: Choose one child with your mentor and learn about their experience of a short game.
steps: Agree a brief observation period and your role with the lead coach.
Describe involvement, choices, waiting and attempts. Avoid fixed labels.
Ask one simple question about the child’s experience.
Share the observation and response with your mentor.
Agree one coaching response and a time to revisit it.
tasks.reflectionPrompt: What did I observe, what did the child tell me, and what assumption changed? What will I check next time? Use an anonymous description: do not include a child’s name or identifying personal details.

tasks.title: Try one adaptation
tasks.prompt: Use one support or challenge for an individual child, with an intended effect and mentor observation.
steps: Choose a resource and identify the child’s current experience with your mentor.
State one intended effect without promising an outcome.
Explain and try one suitable change.
Observe before and after; ask how the change felt.
Discuss alternative explanations; agree whether to keep, change or remove it.
Revisit the idea at a later session.
tasks.reflectionPrompt: What changed in involvement or decisions? What remains uncertain, and what will I try or observe next? Use an anonymous description: do not include a child’s name or identifying personal details.

tasks.title: Assist with a clear purpose
tasks.prompt: Take one agreed supporting role while the lead coach runs an activity.
steps: Confirm role, boundaries, safety briefing and route for help.
Help a child understand the start without changing agreed rules.
Notice a purposeful attempt and offer specific encouragement.
Share one observation with the lead coach afterwards.
Ask your mentor for feedback and agree the next supervised step.
tasks.reflectionPrompt: What helped a child participate? Where did I need help, and what feedback will I apply next time? Use an anonymous description: do not include a child’s name or identifying personal details.

research.title: Coaching Games: Comparisons and Contrasts (Price et al., 2019)
research.application: Teach coaches to choose and justify tools for the child and learning objective.
research.limitation: The proposed metacognitive benefits require empirical investigation; this is not a comparative effectiveness trial.

research.title: Observations of youth football training (OConnor et al., 2017)
research.application: Include an observation task on waiting, listening, transitions and individual involvement.
research.limitation: Descriptive observation of two sessions per coach; does not demonstrate that a specific intervention improves learning.

research.title: The Fun Integration Theory (Visek et al., 2015)
research.application: Ask each child about their experience; enjoyment can include effort and challenge.
research.limitation: Regional sample spanning U9 and older; not a retention trial or a universal ranking for every child.

research.title: The Impact of Nonlinear Pedagogy on Decision-Making and Execution (Praxedes et al., 2018)
research.application: Adapt challenge deliberately, measure the targeted action, and retain flexibility.
research.limitation: Small non-random groups differed in mean age; findings are action-specific and do not establish the best method for all children.

research.title: Effect of a theory-based coach education program on motivational climate: PAPA project (Tzioumakis et al., 2026)
research.application: Include mentoring, refresher tasks and observation across the season.
research.limitation: Nine coaches lost to follow-up; almost all male; observer outcomes do not establish player retention or effectiveness of an online hub.
